name: CT-03
label: Safe D

key_factors: Rosa DeLauro is a long-serving incumbent with strong name recognition
District leans Democratic by 8 points on partisanship
DeLauro has raised over $1.1 million versus about $15,000 for her opponent
Prediction markets price DeLauro at roughly 94% to win
model.rationale: Every available signal points the same way: the seat sits in a Democratic-leaning district, DeLauro is a well-funded incumbent, and her challenger has raised almost nothing. Markets and fundamentals agree this is not competitive.
model.watch: A major late outside-spending intervention or an unexpected incumbent scandal would be the only plausible way this race tightens.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Rosa DeLauro, one of the House's longest-serving Democrats, seeks another term in a Connecticut district that leans Democratic by about eight points. Her Republican challenger, Chris Lancia, has run a minimal campaign, raising roughly $15,000 against DeLauro's more than $1.1 million, with no outside groups engaged on either side. Prediction markets give DeLauro about a 94% chance of winning.

With no public polls and no expert ratings of the race, the forecast rests on fundamentals: the district's partisan lean, incumbency, and the lopsided financial gap. All point to an easy DeLauro win, with the main uncertainty being turnout rather than the outcome itself.
